mechanism_narrative: Joint recovery of workplace and transit mobility from the t-1 trough indicates commuting and discretionary travel are resuming; retail footfall follows with a four-week lag, raising RETAIL_REC above its last four-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -46.4 to -23.1 and TRANSIT from -48.6 to -34.1 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: If both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continue rising over the next four weeks but mean RETAIL_REC is not higher than its last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Residential mobility easing from its peak signals reduced stay-at-home intensity; as residents spend more time outside, discretionary retail visits increase over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 18.3 at t-1w to 12.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL continues declining but mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to its last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week transit rebound exceeding ten points signals policy relaxation or reduced infection fear; retail and recreation mobility rises within two weeks as trips resume.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves more than 10 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved 14.5 points from -48.6 at t-1w to -34.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT again improves more than 10 points week-on-week but mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than its last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent workplace mobility below -20 indicates continued remote-work mandates and suppressed commuter spending; retail and recreation remain below their last four-week mean over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES stays below -20 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES was -31.6 at t-2w, -46.4 at t-1w, and -23.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES remains below -20 for two consecutive weeks but mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than its last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Residential mobility above +10 signals sustained stay-at-home behavior; high home presence suppresses trips to retail and recreation over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL was above +10 in all four observed weeks, ending at 12.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL stays above +10 but mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than its last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Grocery and pharmacy mobility returning to baseline indicates essential-trip normalization and reduced infection fear; broader retail and recreation follow with a four-week lag.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from -4.1 at t-1w to -0.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM remains near zero but mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than its last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: A workplace recovery without a comparable transit recovery indicates continued aversion to public transport, limiting retail trips; retail remains below its last four-week mean over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -30 while WORKPLACES rises above -25
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT was -34.1 and WORKPLACES was -23.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT remains below -30 while WORKPLACES rises above -25 but mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than its last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Parks mobility below -15 signals cold weather suppressing outdoor recreation, which redirects some activity to indoor retail and recreation venues within one week.
failure_condition: If PARKS stays below -15 but mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to its last 28-day mean.
